name: Tuist (module cache)
baseline: xcodebuild clean build with no cache
verdict_reason: In Tuist's public hyperfine runs, replacing unchanged modules with cached binaries cut clean builds 2-3x on three projects, and matched or beat Xcode 26's local compilation cache. The numbers hold for Tuist-generated projects; they are Tuist's own measurements of its own product.
tier_reason: Public benchmark repository with workflow runs and hyperfine output; the accompanying post names Namespace M4 Pro runners and Xcode 26.0.1.
claimed_speedup: Tuist CLI 110.141 s to 34.936 s, Tuist App 68.049 s to 28.080 s, Mastodon (generated) 51.485 s to 24.999 s mean clean build (3.2x, 2.4x and 2.1x, derived from page data)
workload: Clean builds of the Tuist CLI, the Tuist app and Mastodon iOS (as a Tuist-generated project), 5 runs each, module cache including generation and binary fetch
install: mise or Homebrew; project generation with tuist generate
one_liner: Xcode project generator whose module cache swaps unchanged targets for prebuilt binaries, cutting clean builds 2-3x in its benchmarks.
how_it_is_fast: Before generating the Xcode project, Tuist fetches prebuilt frameworks and libraries for every module whose inputs are unchanged and links against them instead of including their sources. The build system then compiles only what changed, and the generated project has fewer targets for Xcode to load. Caching whole modules removes more work than caching individual compiler invocations.
use_it_when: Projects already generated with Tuist, or willing to move to generated projects
Modular apps where most modules are unchanged between builds
CI and local clean builds where a shared cache can be populated
skip_it_when: Projects that must stay hand-maintained .xcodeproj files
Plain SwiftPM-integrated projects: Tuist's own numbers show smaller gains there
caveats: First-party benchmark: Tuist measuring its own product, which it sells as a hosted service
Only 5 runs per configuration; the README itself omits hardware, which is in the blog post
All three module-cache projects are Tuist-generated; no hand-written Xcode project was tested with the module cache
tradeoffs: Requires adopting Tuist's manifest-based project generation
The remote cache needs Tuist's server (hosted, or self-hosted under MPL-2.0); the CLI is MIT, but GitHub reports the repository license as NOASSERTION because of the mixed licensing
Debugging into cached binaries is harder than into source targets
